title: Freeze parser-core unification design
goal: Freeze one parser-core algorithm, precedence authority, migration boundary, and executable acceptance matrix before production changes.
description: Scope: the complete OPT-C group design and executable acceptance artifacts. Context: Parser.cpp mixes recursive-descent layers, ordinal-based arithmetic precedence, postfix special cases, while NewParserExpr.cpp already has a bounded subset precedence loop. Target: select the smallest coherent unification that preserves accepted grammar, exact diagnostics, associativity, nightly-only authority, and bounded resource use. Design Considerations: compare direct precedence climbing with mature LLVM and rust-analyzer Pratt designs plus the local pattern catalog. Constraints & Risks: no new syntax, legacy fallback, Sema/lowering/runtime change, or OPT-D/E work.
conditions: Production implementation may not start until precedence, associativity, recovery, stack-depth, allocation, equivalence, shadow, and zero-fallback evidence are frozen.
